entities.summary: Jelenia Góra is a historic city in southwestern Poland, within the historical region of Lower Silesia. Jelenia Góra is situated in the Lower Silesian Voivodeship, close to the Karkonosze mountain range running along the Polish-Czech border – ski resorts such as Karpacz and Szklarska Poręba are situated 10 to 15 kilometres from the city. Jelenia Góra constitutes a separate urban gmina as well as being the seat of surrounding Karkonosze County. In 2021 the population of Jelenia Góra was 77,366. The area, including the oldest spa district of Cieplice Śląskie-Zdrój, is one of the most valued recreational and leisure locations in Poland.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Jelenia Góra's historical significance lies in its role as a major spa destination during the Classical era, attracting visitors from across Europe. By the mid-19th century, Cieplice Śląskie-Zdrój had become one of the most prominent health resorts in Poland.
